text:
ryan: Thinking out loud — we should build a small synthesis harness that composes: steady background QPS + micro-surges + correlated KV cold starts. Want realistic operator-observable behavior (latency spikes, kernel selection flips, batching tail effects).

anna: +1. can we avoid just replaying traces? need paramized generator so we can do apples-to-apples across kernels.

marta: Agree. My wishlist: (1) stratified user cohorts (few hot keys, many cold), (2) temporal clustering for surges, (3) configurable seq-len and prompt prefix to trigger different kernel paths.

sam: sketch of a config proto:
```yaml
background_qps: 50
surge:
  - start_after: 120   # sec
    duration: 8
    peak_qps: 400
    shape: mixture
cohorts:
  heavy_hitters: {fraction: 0.02, key_pop: pareto(alpha:1.2)}
  casual: {fraction: 0.98, key_pop: uniform}
prefix_cache_ttl: 300
seq_len_dist: {type: gamma, k:2, theta:64}
```

devon: Nice. Two notes: (A) kernel selection boundary around 512 tokens — we should explicitly sweep seq_len to see where runtime chooses different kernels; (B) batching heuristic interacts with micro-surges badly: when batcher waits for more requests it amplifies tail.

ryan: Exactly — we need a metric set: p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel-switch count, avg batch size, KV hit-rate, cost-per-token estimate. Also capture stack traces or perf counters when spikes happen.

anna: For KV cold starts — model the sequence: cold key first request -> KV miss -> populate -> subsequent hits. But also correlate with surge windows so cold-starts coincide with higher QPS.

marta: Also include a mode that injects small background noise of dep vars (e.g., slow storage reads) so we can see how fallback routing behaves.

sam: Implemented a quick prototype that produces a time-series of arrival times + user ids + seq_len. Example generator call:
```
python synth_gen.py --duration 600 --bg-qps 30 --surge "120,8,400" --cohorts config.yaml --seed 42 > arrivals.jsonl
```

devon: Good. When we replay, make sure we run the same arrival file across kernels/quant modes and pin batching config. That gives apples-to-apples.

ci-bot: deploy-check: loadgen harness jenkins job exists: run/synth-replay-e2e. Note it currently uses poisson arrivals only.

ryan: Action items:
- sam: add stratified key-population and pareto heavy-hitter sampling (ETA 1d)
- anna: add seq_len sweep harness and automatic kernel-switch detector (ETA 2d)
- marta: define 3 surge archetypes (micro-spike, sustained ramp, plateau-with-churn) and put into config library (ETA 2d)
- devon: add KV miss modeling & storage latency noise to replay tool (ETA 3d)

marta: We should also capture perf regression signals automatically: e.g., if p99 latency for kernel X increases by >10% vs baseline, fail perf gate.

sam: Quick experiment note: when I forced a micro-surge (peak 350 qps for 6s) while seq_len skewed to 600, kernel switch + batching wait caused 18% p99 increase vs same run with seq_len 300. Will dump harness trace.

anna: Please attach the trace and the minimal repro (arrivals.jsonl + runtime config). We'll diff kernel heatmaps.

ryan: Good discussion. Let's aim to have a first reproducible benchmark next week. Keep messages short in the run logs so we can stitch into CI summary. :thumbsup:
